extracted.intended_audience: individual humanities scholars (including independent and junior scholars) preparing an application for NEH Fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the NEH Fellowships program (individual awards to support humanities research and the production of scholarly outputs). Covers eligibility, allowed project topics and deliverables, budget/time limits, required materials, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core evaluation standard: exceptional research, rigorous analysis, clear writing
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH Fellowships are competitive awards granted to individual scholars pursuing projects that embody exceptional research, rigorous analysis, and clear writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate high scholarly quality in research design and execution, intellectual rigor in analysis, and clarity of prose. Projects may be at any stage of development; applicants should show how the project will produce a significant humanities contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate project's value to humanities scholars and/or general audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must clearly articulate a project’s value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the significance, audience(s), and expected impact of the proposed work (for scholars, for broader publics, or both). Use the narrative to justify why this project merits NEH support.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 topical eligibility: American history/culture and Western civilization
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Fellowships competition will only accept projects for research in American history and culture and Western civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive applications must focus on topics in the history, culture, and government of the United States in any period from the Colonial Era to the present, or topics in Western civilization from antiquity to the present. Confirm topical fit before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted project outputs/deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected Output: Book; Critical Edition; Digital Resource or Publication; Other Scholarly Resource; Peer-reviewed Article; Translation with annotations or critical apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships provide time to conduct research or to produce books, monographs, peer‑reviewed articles, e‑books, born‑digital materials, translations with annotations or a critical apparatus, or critical editions resulting from previous research. Describe the planned deliverable in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award amount $60,000 ($5,000 per month). Fellowship awards are paid directly to the applicant, not to their institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests should not exceed the stated maximum and should reflect the six‑ to twelve‑month period of performance. Be aware that awards will be paid to the individual awardee rather than an institutional payroll account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration / period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a project duration between six and twelve months and align the work plan and budget accordingly. Stated project start dates include April 1, 2027 and September 1, 2028 for this cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: One program per deadline restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply to only one program at each deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must select a single NEH program for submission at each deadline; do not submit the same proposal to multiple NEH programs for the same deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and Program Announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity and the Program Announcement for Fellowships to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and are prepared to write an effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow all formatting, eligibility, content, and submission rules in the current NOFO and Program Announcement. Failure to follow these materials can render an application incomplete or ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application materials and program resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Application Materials: Fellowships 2026 Program Announcement (PDF); Notice of Funding Opportunity (PDF); Grants.gov application package. Program Resources include Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals and Sample Application Narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the listed PDFs and resources when assembling your application. Use sample narratives for orientation only (they are not models); adhere to current NOFO formats and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and submit via Grants.gov; technical submission steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for a Grants.gov account and add an 'individual applicant' profile; follow Grants.gov’s instructions for adding a profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and maintain an active Grants.gov account, add the individual applicant profile, download required software (e.g., Adobe Reader), follow tips for creating valid PDFs, submit the application package on Grants.gov, and verify you receive all submission confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission confirmation and tracking responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive a confirmation from Grants.gov when you’ve successfully submitted your application. Subsequently, you will receive up to five more notices confirming different stages in the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify receipt of all confirmations (watch spam/junk folders). After final Grants.gov confirmation, use the NEH secure site (with your NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number) to monitor status and letters of reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference: timing and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will request letters of reference from your recommenders approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by email when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the status of letters in the NEH secure site; you will see names/emails of letter writers and whether letters have arrived. You are responsible for ensuring letter writers received solicitations and submitted letters; you may send reminders (including the upload link) if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement for independent and junior scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH encourages submissions from independent scholars and junior scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent and early‑career applicants are explicitly invited to apply. Describe qualifications and how the fellowship will advance your research/career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project stage flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may be at any stage of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the project is nascent, mid‑project, or near completion, frame the application to show how the fellowship period will enable meaningful progress or completion of the stated deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals (listed under Program Resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult and comply with NEH’s AI policy as part of proposal preparation and disclosure; follow any instructions in the NOFO regarding AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample narratives are illustrative only
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative samples below are not intended to serve as models, but to give applicants a sense of how a successful application might be crafted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat sample narratives as prescriptive templates; formats or expectations may have changed since those samples were submitted. Always follow current NOFO formatting and content guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program statistics (competition context)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last five competitions this program received an average of 1,033 applications per year; this program has a 7% funding ratio; NEH made an average of 69 awards per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these statistics to understand competitiveness and set realistic expectations; high competition underscores the importance of a clear, compelling application that meets stated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Application available March 2, 2026; Deadline April 22, 2026; Expected notification date January 31, 2027; Project start dates April 1, 2027 and September 1, 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research and deliverable schedules around these dates, and ensure submission and recommender timelines align with NEH's stated schedule.
